title: Coverage Months Carried by a Single Rider Premium Charge
content:
How many coverage months one rider premium charge under the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders carries follows from the member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment — whether that enrollment stands in force, and how often it is billed.

## The rule

**Where the medical plan enrollment the rider hangs on stands in force and is billed quarterly**, the charge carries three coverage months.

**Where that enrollment does not stand in force and a rider premium charge stands on the rider premium account**, the charge carries the whole calendar months from the day the plan received the rider request to the handling date.

**Otherwise**, the charge carries the single coverage month it is booked to.

## Condition and coverage months

| What the Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment shows | What the rider premium account shows | Coverage months carried |
|---|---|---|
| In force, billed quarterly | Anything | 3 |
| In force, billed other than quarterly | Anything | 1 |
| Not in force | At least one rider premium charge standing | The whole calendar months from the day the plan received the rider request to the handling date |
| Not in force | No rider premium charge standing | 1 |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

- A medical plan enrollment standing in force and billed quarterly: the charge carries 3 coverage months, whatever the rider premium account shows.
- A medical plan enrollment no longer standing in force, the rider premium account carrying two charges, and the plan having received the rider request 5 whole calendar months before the handling date: the charge carries 5 coverage months.
- A medical plan enrollment standing in force and billed monthly: the charge carries the single coverage month it is booked to, that is 1.
